items.problem: S9 bounds R13 on one side only, and that is why I16 could be worked and reported while its own measurement stood still. Run by me: `node tools/ui-invariants.mjs --only S9 --break ".browse{width:100% !important}"` fires correctly with ".browse's own right edge (1296.0px) reaches the shell's inner edge (1296.0px) - it did not shrink to its content". But `node tools/ui-invariants.mjs --only S9 --break ".browse{width:240px !important}"` returns ok, and the tool's own banner prints "0 of 1 check(s) fired as intended; 1 did NOT". A .browse shrunk to 240px inside a 1216px shell - leaving 1056px, nearly a whole shell, unoccupied for 3563px - satisfies S9 completely. R13's own text names both edges: at most two declared tracks AND no track's worth of the shell left permanently unoccupied along its full height. S9 enforces only the upper one. This is JUDGE.md L4 recurring in a new dimension: a one-sided geometric invariant passing under opposite-direction displacement. L4 was written about collision corridors; the same failure shape applies to occupancy, and the rule the loop drew from L4 - bound the corridor, not the single edge - was not applied to the invariant written three iterations later.
items.evidence: tools/ui-invariants.mjs --only S9 --break output, both directions, run by me at the current tree; loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/index-wiki--light--1440.png
items.invariant: S9 fails both when .browse's right edge reaches the shell's inner edge AND when it falls below a floor stated as a fraction of the shell's inner width; a --break that shrinks .browse to a fraction of the shell makes S9 fire.
items.prescription: Add the lower bound to S9 and register the falsifier for it in both directions, not only the one the shipped fix happens to move. More generally: JUDGE.md L4's rule should be promoted from a note about sticky collisions to a standing requirement on every geometric invariant this loop registers - if a property is expressed as a comparison between two edges, both directions of displacement must be observed failing before the check is trusted.

items.target: scripts/verify-design.mjs focus sweep, and JUDGE.md rubric section 9's row-10 condition
items.problem: I24 and the accessibility mapping interact, and neither item's invariant can see it. The nav disclosure R14 required is correct, is a genuine tab stop, and the sweep reports it honestly - but the report now reads, on /: 'the complete tab order, 83 stop(s); 84 focusable element(s) in the DOM, 1 of them not currently tabbable (a closed <details> hides its links)', and on /tools: '98 stop(s); 134 focusable element(s) in the DOM, 36 of them not currently tabbable'. The rubric's row 10 requires 'every focus sweep reports swept == total'. With a closed <details> on every route there is now a permanent, correct, by-design gap between swept and total, so swept == total is unreachable and the accessibility ceiling is 8 even after I12 closes. JUDGE.md's own target arithmetic - 8.5 'only if accessibility reaches 10' - is therefore no longer satisfiable by any amount of implementer work. Second, smaller half: three of the four sweeps no longer print the bare '<swept> of <total>' ratio the mapping instructs the judge to read; only /catalog does. The rubric's own escape clause covers this ('If the output does not print a ratio the mapping needs, that is an evidence-fix'). It does not change this verdict's score - /catalog's 0.183 governs either way, and the derivable ratios 83/84, 27/28 and 98/134 are all above 0.5 - but it will govern the next one.

items.problem: The READ column renders the identical string 2026-08-31 on all 396 rows, underlined on every one of them. In current/table-catalog--light--1440.png every visible row's READ cell is the same date carrying the same link treatment as the discriminating MODEL column. A full column of 396 identical underlined strings is chrome by another route: it consumes a seventh of the table's width and a seventh of its rule-crossings while carrying zero discriminating information, and it competes for attention with IN, OUT, CONTEXT and STATUS, which are what a reader crosses the row to compare. Under the revised chrome_restraint test this is the same failure R8's badge clause already forbids for status chips - drawn on every row including the unexceptional ones, so the exceptional case has nothing left to say - applied to a link treatment rather than a border.
items.invariant: No column of a record table renders an identical value on more than 90% of its rows at the same visual weight as the columns a reader compares across; a value constant across the collection is stated once for the collection, not once per row.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R8 (badge clause, by analogy stated explicitly), RULES.md R9
items.prescription: State the read date once in the table's own preamble - the page already says 'last checked 2026-08-31' twice above the filters - and render the READ cell per row only where it differs from that collection default, exactly as the badge clause treats status. If the per-row link target genuinely differs even when the date does not, move the link onto the model name's row-level affordance rather than onto a repeated date string.

On /wiki and /data the cap binds against real content and the same track is correct; the defect is that the track does not respond to the surface it is on.
items.invariant: A .browse surface's label track sizes to that surface's own max-content bounded above by --measure-list, so the gap between the widest rendered label on the surface and the start of the trailing track does not exceed the row gap.
items.prescription: Size the first track as minmax(0, min(max-content, var(--measure-list))) rather than minmax(0, var(--measure-list)). This does not conflict with R13: the track set is still shared across every row of the surface, which is what R13 requires - it is the surface's own content that sets it rather than a global token. Check /data at the same time: its longest label ends at x=436 inside the same 384px-capped track, so /data is the case where the cap correctly binds and must not be loosened.

items.target: app/blog index template, against app/wiki and app/learn
items.problem: The same object - a record-title link on an index - is set at two incompatible measures on the same property. In current/index-blog--light--1440.png the four post titles run from x=259 to x=1278, a 1019px measure, and the third wraps at 1130px; the intro paragraph on that same page is bounded at roughly 605px, so the page contradicts itself. In current/index-wiki--light--1440.png the same object is bounded to a 384px track, and in current/index-learn--light--1440.png to roughly 608px. Three index templates, three measures, one object. A 1019px line of 20px serif is past any reading measure, and it is the widest line of running type anywhere on the property. This is a family-coherence defect, not a taste preference: R7 exists precisely to bound a list's primary label column, and /blog is a list surface that R7's executable form (S1) does not reach because it is not built from .browse-row.
items.invariant: A record-title link on an index template is bounded to the same measure token on every index template of the property; no index sets one past --measure.
items.prescription: Bound the /blog index's title column to --measure-list, the token R7 names, and extend S1's route list to cover /blog so the bound is asserted rather than assumed. If /blog's titles are genuinely too long for --measure-list - three of the four run past 900px - that is an argument for a wider shared token applied to all three indexes, not for one template setting its own; changing the token is in scope for globals.css and changing one template's measure alone is what produced this.

items.target: app/page.tsx home template, the Impossible-to-Routine block (app/globals.css)
items.problem: One decorative accent rule, applied to one of two structurally identical elements. Sampled at x=1250 in current/home--light--1440.png: the 1153px rule above the FIRST pair's heading, at y=1530, is rgb(74,59,212) - full-strength accent - while the same rule above the second pair, at y=1887, is rgb(185,187,199), the property's ordinary neutral. Confirmed in current/home--dark--1440.png at the same coordinates: rgb(156,147,255) against rgb(65,71,87). The coloured rule marks no state and carries no meaning: it separates two sections that are identical in kind, and its sibling separating the identical thing is neutral. The rubric reserves colour for state and meaning, and all three benchmarks agree on that; this is colour as decoration, applied inconsistently, on the site's front door. It is also the only place on the property where a full-strength accent is used as a large area of ink rather than as a link or a chip. NOT SCORED AGAINST colour_discipline: I measured the same pixel in evidence/iter-01/home--light--1440.png (y=1642) and evidence/baseline/home--light--1440.png (y=1666) and it is present in both, so it predates the anchor and no change since made it worse. It is a finding the anchor missed, not a regression.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/home--light--1440.png and home--dark--1440.png, pixel sample at x=1250, y=1530 and y=1887, both themes; compared against evidence/iter-01/ and evidence/baseline/
items.invariant: Two instances of the same structural element within one section render the same rule colour, and a section-separating rule uses the neutral rule token rather than --accent.
items.prescription: Make the first pair's rule neutral like its sibling. If the colour was marking something real - the most recent pair, say - it needs to be marking it on whichever pair is actually most recent and needs a second signal that says what it means; as it stands nothing in the page explains it and no other pair can ever receive it. I checked RULES.md before filing and found no rule governing decorative rule colour, which is why governing_rule is null: R9 governs the resting colour of record LINKS and says --accent marks hover and focus, not resting state, but it does not reach a rule element. If this is fixed, the R9 principle is the natural place to widen.

items.problem: Unchanged and not worked, but the anchor overstated it and I am correcting the measurement rather than carrying the number. Measured at 1440x900: .home-side's bottom edge is at y=646.5 while .rail-changes runs to y=1334.6 on a 2559px page, so the empty right column is about 690px, not the ~2000px the anchor recorded. It is still 690px of empty column beside the site's front-door content, and it is the same defect as I16 on a template that HAS a second track and stops filling it a quarter of the way down.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/home--light--1440.png and home--dark--1440.png; measurement by judge-run Playwright at 1440x900
items.invariant: On the home page at 1440x900, the right rail's content extends to at least 60% of the changed feed's own height, or the feed reflows to use the full shell below the rail's end.
items.prescription: Let the changed feed reflow into the full shell width once the rail ends, rather than holding a 366px column open beside nothing. Adding more rail content is a content change and slot 1 forbids it, so the presentation-only remedy is the reflow. R6 constrains this: whatever is done, changed-feed lines must still be visible above the fold at both 1440x900 and 390x844.

items.problem: Unchanged. 38 of the 40 captures are fullPage images taken at scroll position 0, so nothing scroll-linked is observable from the set - JUDGE.md L3. This iteration it cost something specific: I25's remedy is a scroll-dependent property (the gap between the wrap and the footer at maximum scroll) and no capture in the set can show it. I verified it with my own Playwright measurement instead, which is the right escalation but means the screenshot oracle contributed nothing to judging the item.
items.invariant: For every route whose layout is scroll-coupled, the evidence set contains at least one capture at a non-zero scroll position, labelled with the scroll offset in the manifest.
items.prescription: Add a scrolled capture for /catalog at 1440 and for / at 390 - the two routes with known scroll-coupled properties - and record the scroll offset in the manifest entry beside capture and buildStamp.

items.problem: Unchanged. The viewport-coupled detector is keyed to one CSS signature - an element whose computed position is sticky and whose max-height is vh-based - so it catches the one case already known and would not catch a second instance built differently. The general assertion filed alongside I22 (that a fullPage capture be verified to render the page faithfully, not merely to capture the right page) was not implemented. state.md D9's own statement of the lesson - identity is not fidelity - is broader than the check that was built from it.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/manifest.json - only the two /catalog 1440 entries carry capture: "viewport"; tools/ui-evidence.mjs detector
items.invariant: For every capture, the manifest records a comparison between a geometry measured live in the page and the same geometry measured in the rendered image, and refuses the capture when they disagree beyond a stated tolerance.
items.prescription: Compare one measured height taken from the live DOM against the same element's height located in the produced PNG, per capture, rather than pattern-matching the CSS that happens to have caused the one known instance. I checked RULES.md and found no rule governing evidence fidelity - the lesson lives in JUDGE.md L5 and state.md D9 as narrative only, which is why governing_rule is null and why the check drifted narrower than the lesson.

items.problem: Unchanged and still unresolvable by this loop. /catalog presents 396 rows as one continuous surface with four filter controls and no pagination or grouping. Whether a reader can find one model among 396 by filtering rather than by paging is a question about a real person's behaviour, which no screenshot and no DOM invariant answers. Listed so it stops resurfacing as actionable.
